title: Absolute ampleness in a finite quasi-projective tower
statement: Let S be an affine Noetherian scheme, B a Noetherian scheme, and b:B→S and p:V→B morphisms. Assume p is locally of finite type and quasi-compact [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and both b and p admit immersions into finite-dimensional projective spaces over their respective targets [def-per-gabber-modification-data]. Then V admits an invertible module L [def-sc-invertible-module] which is absolutely ample [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module]. This asserts no group action or quotient.

proof.text: Compose the given immersions by base changing B→P^m_S along P^n, identifying the result with P^n_S times_S P^m_S, and applying the closed Segre embedding. Reindex the finite nonempty product of coordinate types by ULift(Fin(d+1)). The composite is an immersion over S. This is the proved private helper quasiProjective_comp, not an assumed composition theorem.

source.place: Tags 01WD, 01NE; quotient original Step 1, replacement of the relative-twist route

proof.text: Identify the affine S with Spec Γ(S,⊤). Apply the projective ample theorem to the identity closed immersion of the finite-dimensional projective space. This supplies an actual ample invertible module N on that ambient scheme.

For each source point choose an affine positive-power section locus of N containing its image and contained in the coborder open of the immersion, using the finite-principal-affine theorem on the singleton. The immersion is closed inside that coborder, so this affine open has affine inverse image. The tensor-power section pullback theorem gives a section of the pulled-back module with exactly that inverse-image locus. Invertibility is preserved by pullback. These are the pointwise clauses of the absolute ample criterion.

proof.text: The top scheme V is quasi-compact since p is quasi-compact and B is Noetherian. Together with the preceding section loci this proves absolute ampleness. For empty V the pointwise condition is vacuous.
